is [high] The turn prompt injects untrusted document really an issue if the document was generated from scratch by agent?

> AGENT

Honestly, not really in this context. Codex is applying the prompt injection rule generically without considering the actual trust model here.

The threat model for prompt injection is **untrusted input from outside the system** — user-submitted forms, external API responses, documents from unknown sources. In this design:

- Both agents are operating under your authority on your local machine
- The document is created from scratch by those same agents
- The summaries are written by the agents themselves
- You're actively watching and steering

There's no real trust boundary being crossed. Agent A's output going into Agent B's prompt is not meaningfully different from an agent reading a file it previously wrote.

**The one edge case worth noting:** if you paste external content into the document (e.g., copy from a PR, an external spec, or a web page), that content does flow into the next agent's prompt. But that's true of any tool that reads files — it's not specific to this design, and you made the conscious choice to add that content.

I'd say: acknowledge it in the spec as a known consideration but don't add structural mitigation. A simple note like "the turn prompt treats document content as data context, not instructions" in the prompt template is sufficient. The other two findings (fencing tokens and snapshot cleanup) are more actionable. Want me to address those?

130	WAIT    → Free to do other work — skills, questions, anything
131	```
132	
133	### Step Details
134	
135	**WAIT — Polling vs. Notification**
136	- Dual-session mode: agent polls `state.json` on a short interval (~60s). Between polls, the agent is free — user can invoke other skills, ask questions, do anything.
137	- Orchestrator mode: the orchestrating agent manages turn transitions directly — no polling needed. It dispatches the other agent, waits for completion, then updates state.
138	
139	**CLAIM — Preventing Races**
140	Agent writes its identity + timestamp to `state.json` before starting work. If two agents race to claim, the last writer wins — the other detects the conflict on its next read and backs off.
141	
142	**READ — Context Building**
143	Agent reads the full document plus the diff from the previous turn. To compute the diff: retrieve the previous version via `git cat-file -p <prev_content_hash>` and diff it against the current file. The skill includes this diff in the turn prompt so the agent sees both the current state and what specifically changed.
144	
145	**EDIT — Document Modification**
146	Agent makes changes guided by its role (if set) or a generic "improve the document" directive. No commits — just file edits.
147	
148	**HANDOFF — State Transition**
149	After editing, agent runs `git hash-object -w <document_path>` to capture the new content hash (the `-w` flag writes the blob to the object store so it can be retrieved later for diffs), writes a one-line summary of what it changed, updates `state.json` with the next agent in `turn_order`, increments `turn.number`, and appends to `history[]`. If `max_turns` is set and reached, sets `status = "completed"`.
150	
151	### Lease Expiry & Recovery
152	
153	If `now - turn.started_at > lease_seconds`, the turn is expired. Any agent (or the user) can reclaim it. The expired turn gets a history entry marked `"expired": true` with no content hash. The document may be partially edited — the next agent works from whatever state the file is in.
154	
155	### Diffs Without Commits
156	
157	Each history entry stores a git blob hash (`git hash-object -w <file>` — the `-w` flag writes the blob to the object store so it persists). To see what changed between turns:
158	
159	```bash
160	# Retrieve previous turn's version
161	git cat-file -p <prev_turn_hash> > /tmp/prev-version.md
162	
163	# Diff against current file
164	diff /tmp/prev-version.md docs/design.md
165	
166	# Or diff between any two turns
167	git cat-file -p <turn1_hash> > /tmp/t1.md
168	git cat-file -p <turn2_hash> > /tmp/t2.md
169	diff /tmp/t1.md /tmp/t2.md
170	```
171	
172	The skill handles this automatically — agents receive the diff as part of their turn prompt.
173	
174	### Checkpoint Integration
175	
176	**During collaboration:** Entire's temporary checkpoints fire automatically on agent TurnEnd hooks. These capture the working tree (including uncommitted document edits) on shadow branches. Recovery is possible even without any commits.
177	
178	**When user commits:** Entire condensation creates a committed checkpoint with the full collaboration history. Searchable via `entire search`, explainable via `entire explain`.
179

107	### Key Design Decisions
108	
109	- **`.entire/collab/` is gitignored** — state file is ephemeral coordination, not committed. The document and Entire checkpoints are the durable record.
110	- **Lease-based turns** — each turn has a `lease_seconds` timeout (default 120s). If an agent crashes or stalls, the lease expires and the other agent (or user) can reclaim the turn.
111	- **History is append-only** — every turn gets a history entry with its content hash, linking the fast coordination layer to the durable checkpoint layer.
112	- **Agent-agnostic `type` field** — uses Entire's `AgentType` values. Works with any agent.
113	- **Content hashes for diffs** — each history entry stores a `git hash-object` of the document. Next agent diffs between hashes to see what changed, no commits needed.

1	# Collab Skill — Multi-Agent Document Collaboration
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-04-14
4	**Status:** Draft
5	**Author:** Alisha Kawaguchi + Claude
6	
7	## Overview
8	
9	A skill that enables multiple AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, etc.) to collaboratively author and refine a shared document through turn-based editing. Agents take short turns — one writes while the other reads/thinks — creating a sense of concurrency. The user can steer, pause, redirect, and stop the collaboration at any time, and other skills remain fully usable throughout.
10	
11	## Requirements
12	
13	- **Concurrent collaboration** with turn-based short leases — one agent writes while the other reads/thinks
14	- **Two modes**: single orchestrator (one terminal) or dual session (two terminals, shared protocol)
15	- **Single markdown file** as the shared document
16	- **General-purpose** — any document type, not just specs
17	- **Optional role assignment** at kickoff, with ability to interject/redirect mid-session
18	- **Agent-agnostic** — works with any agent that has file read/write and shell access
19	- **Termination**: fixed turn count or user-controlled stop
20	- **Non-blocking** — must coexist with other skills (brainstorming, etc.) within the same session
21	- **Uses existing Entire CLI infrastructure** — temporary checkpoints, session state, hooks
22	- **No commits required during collaboration** — user commits when satisfied
23	
24	## Architecture: Hybrid State File + Checkpoints
25	
26	Two coordination layers:
27	
28	1. **Fast path — `.entire/collab/<collab_id>/state.json`**: Local state file for real-time turn coordination. Not committed to git. Readable by any agent.
29	2. **Durable path — Entire temporary checkpoints**: Fire automatically on agent TurnEnd hooks. Capture working tree state (including uncommitted document edits) on shadow branches. Enable recovery without commits.
30	
31	When the user commits, Entire condensation creates a committed checkpoint with the full collaboration history, searchable via `entire search` and explainable via `entire explain`.
32	
33	If the state file is lost, the skill reconstructs state from checkpoint history.
34	
35	## Collaboration State Protocol
36	
37	### Directory Structure
38	
39	```
40	project/
41	├── .entire/
42	│   └── collab/
43	│       └── <collab_id>/
44	│           ├── state.json           ← coordination file (gitignored)
45	│           └── snapshots/           ← turn snapshots (cleaned up on stop)
46	│               ├── turn-1.md
47	│               ├── turn-2.md
48	│               └── turn-3.md
49	├── docs/
50	│   └── design.md                   ← shared document (user chooses path)
51	└── .gitignore                       ← .entire/ added here
52	```
53	
54	Multiple concurrent collaborations are supported — each gets its own `collab_id` directory.
55	
56	### state.json Schema
57	
58	```json
59	{
60	  "collab_id": "a8f3c921",
61	  "document_path": "docs/design.md",
62	  "status": "active | paused | completed",
63	  "mode": "orchestrated | dual-session",
64	
65	  "turn": {
66	    "number": 3,
67	    "agent": "codex",
68	    "version": 7,
69	    "started_at": "2026-04-14T10:02:00Z",
70	    "lease_seconds": 120
71	  },
72	
73	  "agents": [
74	    {
75	      "type": "claude-code",
76	      "session_id": "019d...",
77	      "role": "Draft architecture",
78	      "turns_completed": 1
79	    },
80	    {
81	      "type": "codex",
82	      "session_id": "a4e2...",
83	      "role": "Review edge cases",
84	      "turns_completed": 1
85	    }
86	  ],
87	
88	  "config": {
89	    "max_turns": null,
90	    "turn_order": ["claude-code", "codex"]
91	  },
92	
93	  "history": [
94	    {
95	      "turn": 1,
96	      "agent": "claude-code",
97	      "snapshot": "snapshots/turn-1.md",
98	      "summary": "Drafted architecture overview",
99	      "timestamp": "2026-04-14T10:01:30Z"
100	    },
101	    {
102	      "turn": 2,
103	      "agent": "codex",
104	      "snapshot": "snapshots/turn-2.md",
105	      "summary": "Added caching layer, flagged missing auth",
106	      "timestamp": "2026-04-14T10:02:00Z"
107	    }
108	  ]
109	}
110	```
111	
112	### Key Design Decisions
113	
114	- **`.entire/collab/` is gitignored** — state file is ephemeral coordination, not committed. The document and Entire checkpoints are the durable record.
115	- **Lease-based turns** — each turn has a `lease_seconds` timeout (default 120s). If an agent crashes or stalls, the lease expires and the other agent (or user) can reclaim the turn.
116	- **History is append-only** — every turn gets a history entry with its content hash, linking the fast coordination layer to the durable checkpoint layer.
117	- **Agent-agnostic `type` field** — uses Entire's `AgentType` values. Works with any agent.
118	- **Snapshot files for diffs** — each turn's document state is copied to `.entire/collab/<id>/snapshots/turn-<N>.md`. Plain files with explicit cleanup on session end — no git object store bloat.
119	- **Fenced turn ownership** — `turn.version` acts as a fencing token. CLAIM and HANDOFF both verify the version hasn't changed (compare-and-swap), preventing split-brain state from races or expired leases.
120	
121	## Turn Lifecycle
122	
123	### Turn Flow
124	
125	```
126	WAIT    → Read state.json — is it my turn?
127	          ↓ yes (or lease expired)
128	CLAIM   → Write state: turn.agent = me, turn.started_at = now
129	          ↓
130	READ    → Read document + diff from previous turn's content hash
131	          ↓
132	EDIT    → Make changes to the document (using role/directive if set)
133	          ↓
134	HANDOFF → Hash document, update state: next agent, append history
135	          ↓ Entire TurnEnd hook fires → temporary checkpoint
136	WAIT    → Free to do other work — skills, questions, anything
137	```
138	
139	### Step Details
140	
141	**WAIT — Polling vs. Notification**
142	- Dual-session mode: agent polls `state.json` on a short interval (~60s). Between polls, the agent is free — user can invoke other skills, ask questions, do anything.
143	- Orchestrator mode: the orchestrating agent manages turn transitions directly — no polling needed. It dispatches the other agent, waits for completion, then updates state.
144	
145	**CLAIM — Fenced Turn Ownership**
146	Agent reads `state.json` and records the current `turn.version`. To claim the turn, it writes its identity, timestamp, and increments `turn.version` atomically. Before writing, it re-reads the file and verifies `turn.version` has not changed since it was read (compare-and-swap). If the version has changed, another agent claimed first — back off and re-enter WAIT.
147	
148	**READ — Context Building**
149	Agent reads the full document plus the diff from the previous turn. To compute the diff: read the previous turn's snapshot from `.entire/collab/<id>/snapshots/turn-<N-1>.md` and diff it against the current file. The skill includes this diff in the turn prompt so the agent sees both the current state and what specifically changed.
150	
151	**EDIT — Document Modification**
152	Agent makes changes guided by its role (if set) or a generic "improve the document" directive. No commits — just file edits.
153	
154	**HANDOFF — Fenced State Transition**
155	Before writing the handoff, agent re-reads `state.json` and verifies it still owns the turn (`turn.version` matches what it set during CLAIM). If the version has changed (e.g., lease was reclaimed), the agent aborts — its edits remain in the file but it does not update state. If the version matches, the agent: copies the document to `.entire/collab/<collab_id>/snapshots/turn-<N>.md` as a snapshot, writes a one-line summary, increments `turn.version` and `turn.number`, sets the next agent in `turn_order`, and appends to `history[]`. If `max_turns` is set and reached, sets `status = "completed"`.
156	
157	### Lease Expiry & Recovery
158	
159	If `now - turn.started_at > lease_seconds`, the turn is expired. Any agent (or the user) can reclaim it using the same fenced CLAIM protocol — read the current `turn.version`, verify, increment, and write. The expired turn gets a history entry marked `"expired": true` with no snapshot. If the original agent completes after its lease was reclaimed, its HANDOFF version check fails and it aborts gracefully — its file edits remain but state is not corrupted. The next agent works from whatever state the file is in.
160	
161	### Diffs Without Commits
162	
163	Each turn's HANDOFF step copies the document to `.entire/collab/<collab_id>/snapshots/turn-<N>.md`. These snapshot files are plain copies — no git object store involvement. To see what changed between turns:
164	
165	```bash
166	# Diff between turn 1 and turn 2
167	diff .entire/collab/a8f3c921/snapshots/turn-1.md .entire/collab/a8f3c921/snapshots/turn-2.md
168	
169	# Diff between last turn and current file
170	diff .entire/collab/a8f3c921/snapshots/turn-2.md docs/design.md
171	```
172	
173	The skill handles this automatically — agents receive the diff as part of their turn prompt.
174	
175	**Cleanup:** When a collaboration ends (`/collab stop` or `max_turns` reached), the skill deletes the snapshots directory. Snapshots are ephemeral — the document itself and Entire checkpoints are the durable record.
176	
177	### Checkpoint Integration
178	
179	**During collaboration:** Entire's temporary checkpoints fire automatically on agent TurnEnd hooks. These capture the working tree (including uncommitted document edits) on shadow branches. Recovery is possible even without any commits.
180	
181	**When user commits:** Entire condensation creates a committed checkpoint with the full collaboration history. Searchable via `entire search`, explainable via `entire explain`.
182	
183	## Skill Architecture
184	
185	### Plugin Layout
186	
187	```
188	plugins/entire/skills/
189	└── collab/
190	    ├── SKILL.md                 ← main skill (invocation, protocol, turn logic)
191	    ├── references/
192	    │   ├── state-schema.md      ← state.json format reference
193	    │   └── recovery.md          ← checkpoint recovery procedures
194	    └── agents/
195	        └── collab-worker.md     ← subagent for orchestrator mode
196	```
197	
198	### Two Modes
199	
200	**Mode A: Orchestrator** — one terminal, skill manages both agents.
201	- User invokes `/collab start <doc>` and chooses orchestrated mode.
202	- Claude Code takes its turns directly, dispatches Codex via the existing `codex:rescue` / companion script.
203	- For non-Codex agents, the orchestrator writes the turn state and tells the user to trigger the agent manually (falls back to dual-session behavior for that agent).
204	- Turn transitions are automatic — no polling.
205	
206	**Mode B: Dual Session** — two (or more) terminals, each agent runs the skill independently.
207	- First agent invokes `/collab start <doc>`, subsequent agents invoke `/collab join <doc>`.
208	- Each agent polls `state.json` on ~60s intervals.
209	- Between polls, the session is completely free for other work.
210	- Not limited to 2 agents — `turn_order` rotates through however many join.
211	
212	### Skill Commands
213	
214	| Command | Description |
215	|---------|-------------|
216	| `/collab start <doc-path>` | Initialize state, create doc, take first turn (or wait) |
217	| `/collab join <doc-path>` | Join existing collaboration session |
218	| `/collab status` | Show current state: whose turn, turn count, agents |
219	| `/collab pause` | Pause collaboration (both agents stop claiming turns) |
220	| `/collab resume` | Resume paused collaboration |
221	| `/collab stop` | End collaboration, keep document as-is |
222	| `/collab redirect <agent> <directive>` | Change an agent's role mid-session |
223	
224	### Invocation Parameters
225	
226	On `/collab start`, the skill prompts for (all optional, has defaults):
227	
228	| Parameter | Options | Default |
229	|-----------|---------|---------|
230	| Mode | orchestrated / dual-session | dual-session |
231	| Agents | list of agent types | auto-detect via `entire sessions list` |
232	| Max turns | number or null | null (unlimited) |
233	| Roles | per-agent directives | none (generic improve) |
234	| Lease | seconds per turn | 120 |
235	
236	### Non-Blocking Design
237	
238	The skill does not take over the session. When it's not your turn:
239	
240	- Use `/brainstorm`, `/commit`, or any other skill
241	- Ask questions, explore code
242	- Edit other files
243	- Run tests, builds, anything
244	- Manually edit the collab document
245	
246	Turn detection in dual-session mode uses periodic polling (~60s). In orchestrator mode, transitions are automatic after the dispatched agent completes.
247	
248	## Agent Integration
249	
250	### Agent Requirements
251	
252	For an agent to participate, it needs exactly one capability:
253	
254	1. **Read & write files** — read `state.json`, read the document, edit the document, copy the document to a snapshot file, write updated state.
255	
256	No SDK, no API, no git commands, no special hooks. The protocol is just files.
257	
258	### Per-Agent Behavior
259	
260	**Claude Code:** SKILL.md loaded natively via plugin. Polls via `/loop` or `ScheduleWakeup`. Edits via Edit tool. Can orchestrate other agents via `codex:rescue` companion or Agent tool.
261	
262	**Codex:** SKILL.md in `.codex-plugin` or instructions delivered via companion prompt. Reads state.json via shell. In orchestrator mode, typically the dispatched agent rather than the orchestrator.
263	
264	**Any other agent (Gemini, Cursor, etc.):** Agent-specific plugin format or manual instructions. Reads state.json via file access. Protocol is file-based — no agent-specific APIs needed.
265	
266	### Turn Prompt Template
267	
268	When it's an agent's turn, the skill constructs this context:
269	
270	```markdown
271	## Collaboration Turn
272	
273	You are participating in a collaborative document session.
274	
275	Document: docs/api-design.md
276	Your role: Review for edge cases and security concerns
277	Turn: 4 of unlimited
278	Previous agent: claude-code
279	
280	## What changed last turn
281	(diff from turn 3 → current document)
282	+ Added rate limiting section
283	+ Defined retry backoff strategy
284	- Removed deprecated v1 endpoints
285	
286	## Previous turn summaries
287	Turn 1 (claude-code): Drafted initial API structure with CRUD endpoints
288	Turn 2 (codex): Added pagination, error codes, versioning strategy
289	Turn 3 (claude-code): Added rate limiting, retry backoff, removed v1
290	
291	## Instructions
292	1. Read the full document
293	2. Review the diff to understand what changed
294	3. Make your improvements (guided by your role if set)
295	4. Write a one-line summary of what you changed
296	5. Do NOT commit — just edit the file
297	```
298	
299	### Agent Registration
300	
301	On `/collab start` or `/collab join`:
302	
303	1. Skill detects current agent type (from Entire session or environment)
304	2. Adds agent to `state.json → agents[]` with session ID
305	3. Adds agent to `turn_order` (appended, or user specifies position)
306	4. If first agent: takes turn 1. Otherwise: enters WAIT.
307	
308	Agents can join mid-collaboration. New agent is appended to `turn_order` and picks up on the next rotation.
309	
310	## Edge Cases & Recovery
311	
312	| Scenario | Handling |
313	|----------|----------|
314	| **Agent crashes mid-turn** | Lease expires after `lease_seconds`. Next polling agent sees expired lease, reclaims the turn. History entry marked `"expired": true`. Document may be partially edited — next agent works from whatever state the file is in. |
315	| **User edits doc manually** | Allowed. Next agent sees current file state regardless of who edited it. Content hash won't match last turn's hash, so diff includes user's edits. State file doesn't need updating. |
316	| **State file deleted/corrupted** | Skill reconstructs from Entire checkpoint history — reads temporary checkpoints, rebuilds turn order from session metadata, recovers last known document hash. Prompts user to confirm before resuming. |
317	| **Agent makes bad edits** | User can `/collab pause`, manually fix the document or `git checkout` the file, then `/collab resume`. Content hash becomes stale but next agent diffs from current file state. |
318	| **New agent joins mid-collab** | Runs `/collab join`. Gets appended to `turn_order`. Receives full history summaries on first turn. |
319	| **Agent leaves mid-collab** | Removed from `turn_order`. If it was their turn, lease expires and next agent picks up. Remaining agents continue rotating. |
320	| **Multiple collabs at once** | Each collaboration gets its own `state.json` keyed by `collab_id` under `.entire/collab/<collab_id>/`. `/collab status` lists all active sessions. |
321	
```

The spec doesn't explain how any of this metadata is recovered from checkpoint data alone. At best you can recover the document; you cannot recover the collaboration session state. The edge case table (line 316) repeats this claim without additional detail.",
      "recommendation": "Either: (1) stop gitignoring state.json so it's captured in checkpoints, or (2) drop the recovery claim and instead say 'if state is lost, the collaboration must be restarted — the document itself is preserved.' Option 2 is honest and simple. Option 1 adds committed collab metadata to the repo, which you explicitly wanted to avoid."
    }
  ]
}
```

---

Three findings. The first two are structural — the fencing mechanism and the multi-step HANDOFF both have real gaps. The third is an honesty issue — the spec promises recovery it can't deliver.

The TOCTOU race (#1) is worth deciding on now: do you want real atomicity (rename-from-tmpfile is easy), or do you want to acknowledge the race is unlikely and add detection instead? For a 2-agent collab with 60s polls, the practical risk is very low, but the spec currently overpromises.

> DEVELOPER

if agent is on auto mode meaning its having it do 8 turns. does this race become more common

> AGENT

No, actually. The race doesn't get worse in auto mode. Here's why:

**The race requires two agents writing state.json at the same millisecond.** Auto mode doesn't change that dynamic:

- **Orchestrator mode (auto):** Fully sequential. The orchestrator dispatches Agent A, waits for it to finish, updates state, dispatches Agent B. One agent active at a time. Zero race window.

- **Dual-session mode (auto):** Agent A finishes, writes HANDOFF. Agent B is polling on a 60s interval, eventually notices, CLAIMs, does its work, writes HANDOFF. Agent A is polling, eventually notices... The polling gap (60s) naturally serializes access. The turns happen faster (no user delay), but they're still one-at-a-time.

The only scenario where the race matters is **lease expiry** — Agent A stalls past its lease, Agent B reclaims the turn via CLAIM, and Agent A wakes up and tries to HANDOFF at the exact same moment. That's the same whether it's auto or manual, and the window is milliseconds.

Given that, I'd say: acknowledge the theoretical race exists, add the simple detection mechanism (check history is monotonically increasing on each READ), but don't over-engineer the atomicity. Want me to update the spec with that framing instead of the current "atomic CAS" language?

> DEVELOPER

explain what this is "do you want real atomicity (rename-from-tmpfile is easy)"

> AGENT

It's a standard pattern for atomic file writes on POSIX systems:

```bash
# Instead of this (NOT atomic — reader can see partial write):
write state.json

# Do this (atomic):
write state.json.tmp      # 1. Write new content to a temp file
mv state.json.tmp state.json  # 2. rename() is atomic on POSIX
```

`rename()` (which `mv` uses) is guaranteed by POSIX to be atomic — the file is either the old version or the new version, never a half-written mess. A reader opening `state.json` will always get a complete, valid file.

So the CLAIM step would be:
1. Read `state.json`, check version
2. Re-read `state.json`, verify version unchanged
3. Write updated state to `state.json.tmp`
4. `mv state.json.tmp state.json`

This doesn't solve the TOCTOU gap between steps 2 and 4 (another agent could still sneak in), but it does guarantee no reader ever sees a corrupt/partial state file. The CAS race is about two agents both passing the version check — rename doesn't fix that. Only `flock()` or a real lock would.

For this design though, I don't think you need either. The race window is milliseconds, agents poll on 60s intervals, and the worst case is a duplicated turn on a design doc. The simpler fix is: drop the "atomic" language, add monotonic history validation on READ (if `history.length` doesn't match what you expect, back off), and call it sufficient.

112	### Key Design Decisions
113	
114	- **`.entire/collab/` is gitignored** — state file is ephemeral coordination, not committed. The document and Entire checkpoints are the durable record.
115	- **Lease-based turns** — each turn has a `lease_seconds` timeout (default 120s). If an agent crashes or stalls, the lease expires and the other agent (or user) can reclaim the turn.
116	- **History is append-only** — every turn gets a history entry with its content hash, linking the fast coordination layer to the durable checkpoint layer.
117	- **Agent-agnostic `type` field** — uses Entire's `AgentType` values. Works with any agent.
118	- **Snapshot files for diffs** — each turn's document state is copied to `.entire/collab/<id>/snapshots/turn-<N>.md`. Plain files with explicit cleanup on session end — no git object store bloat.
119	- **Fenced turn ownership** — `turn.version` acts as a fencing token. CLAIM and HANDOFF both verify the version hasn't changed (compare-and-swap), preventing split-brain state from races or expired leases.
120	
121	## Turn Lifecycle
122	
123	### Turn Flow
124	
125	```
126	WAIT    → Read state.json — is it my turn?
127	          ↓ yes (or lease expired)
128	CLAIM   → Write state: turn.agent = me, turn.started_at = now
129	          ↓
130	READ    → Read document + diff from previous turn's content hash
131	          ↓
132	EDIT    → Make changes to the document (using role/directive if set)
133	          ↓
134	HANDOFF → Hash document, update state: next agent, append history
135	          ↓ Entire TurnEnd hook fires → temporary checkpoint
136	WAIT    → Free to do other work — skills, questions, anything
137	```
138	
139	### Step Details
140	
141	**WAIT — Polling vs. Notification**
142	- Dual-session mode: agent polls `state.json` on a short interval (~60s). Between polls, the agent is free — user can invoke other skills, ask questions, do anything.
143	- Orchestrator mode: the orchestrating agent manages turn transitions directly — no polling needed. It dispatches the other agent, waits for completion, then updates state.
144	
145	**CLAIM — Fenced Turn Ownership**
146	Agent reads `state.json` and records the current `turn.version`. To claim the turn, it writes its identity, timestamp, and increments `turn.version` atomically. Before writing, it re-reads the file and verifies `turn.version` has not changed since it was read (compare-and-swap). If the version has changed, another agent claimed first — back off and re-enter WAIT.
147	
148	**READ — Context Building**
149	Agent reads the full document plus the diff from the previous turn. To compute the diff: read the previous turn's snapshot from `.entire/collab/<id>/snapshots/turn-<N-1>.md` and diff it against the current file. The skill includes this diff in the turn prompt so the agent sees both the current state and what specifically changed.
150	
151	**EDIT — Document Modification**
152	Agent makes changes guided by its role (if set) or a generic "improve the document" directive. No commits — just file edits.
153	
154	**HANDOFF — Fenced State Transition**
155	Before writing the handoff, agent re-reads `state.json` and verifies it still owns the turn (`turn.version` matches what it set during CLAIM). If the version has changed (e.g., lease was reclaimed), the agent aborts — its edits remain in the file but it does not update state. If the version matches, the agent: copies the document to `.entire/collab/<collab_id>/snapshots/turn-<N>.md` as a snapshot, writes a one-line summary, increments `turn.version` and `turn.number`, sets the next agent in `turn_order`, and appends to `history[]`. If `max_turns` is set and reached, sets `status = "completed"`.
156	
157	### Lease Expiry & Recovery
158	
159	If `now - turn.started_at > lease_seconds`, the turn is expired. Any agent (or the user) can reclaim it using the same fenced CLAIM protocol — read the current `turn.version`, verify, increment, and write. The expired turn gets a history entry marked `"expired": true` with no snapshot. If the original agent completes after its lease was reclaimed, its HANDOFF version check fails and it aborts gracefully — its file edits remain but state is not corrupted. The next agent works from whatever state the file is in.
160	
161	### Diffs Without Commits
```

Based on my thorough exploration of `/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/skills/experiment/`, here is the complete file structure and conventions used by existing skills:

### 1. SKILL.md Files (Frontmatter and Content Format)

Optional fields in some skills:

**Content Structure:**
- H1 title (# Skill Name)
- Optional "STOP" section with critical rules (session-handoff uses this)
- Multiple H2 sections for different flows/processes
- H3 subsections for step-by-step instructions
- Code blocks with bash commands and JSON examples

**The three skills:**

**1. session-handoff/SKILL.md** (6,111 bytes) — Reads Entire session transcripts and helps transfer work between agents. Contains three flows: Active/current session, Checkpoint handoff, and bare invocation.

**2. explain/SKILL.md** (1,550 bytes) — Traces source code to original conversations via git blame and `entire explain --commit`. Works with functions, files, and line changes. Minimal, procedural format.

**3. search/SKILL.md** (2,167 bytes) — Finds prior work using `entire search --json`. Supports filters: `--repo`, `--branch`, `--author`, `--date`. Shows search heuristics and failure modes.

    "SessionStart": [{ "matcher": null, "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "entire hooks codex session-start", "timeout": 30 }] }],
    "Stop": [{ "matcher": null, "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "entire hooks codex stop", "timeout": 30 }] }],
    "UserPromptSubmit": [{ "matcher": null, "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "entire hooks codex user-prompt-submit", "timeout": 30 }] }]
  }
}
```

### 5. Agent Configuration

**.claude/agents/entire-search.md** (Claude Code subagent):
```yaml
---
name: entire-search
description: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository.
tools: Bash
model: haiku
---

<!-- ENTIRE-MANAGED SEARCH SUBAGENT v1 -->

[Agent instructions for running `entire search --json` queries]
```

Pattern: Agents are YAML frontmatter + instructions. This agent specifically handles `entire search --json` queries and forces JSON output mode.

### 6. OpenCode Integration

**.opencode/INSTALL.md** — Installation guide that tells users to add to their config:
```json
{ "plugin": ["skills@git+https://github.com/entireio/skills.git"] }
```

**.opencode/plugins/entire.js** — Plugin hook file (ES module) that auto-registers the skills directory:
```javascript
export const EntirePlugin = async ({ client, directory }) => {
  const skillsDir = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../plugins/entire/skills');
  return {
    config: async (config) => {
      config.skills = config.skills || {};
      config.skills.paths = config.skills.paths || [];
      if (!config.skills.paths.includes(skillsDir)) {
        config.skills.paths.push(skillsDir);
      }
    },
  };
};
```

### 7. Gemini Integration

**gemini-extension.json** (Gemini configuration):
```json
{
  "name": "entire",
  "description": "Cross-agent skills and commands powered by Entire.",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "contextFileName": "GEMINI.md"
}
```

**GEMINI.md** (Gemini context file):
```
@./plugins/entire/skills/session-handoff/SKILL.md
```

Pattern: Gemini uses `@` references to include skill files directly.

### 8. Root-Level Configuration

**package.json**:
```json
{
  "name": "skills",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "type": "module",
  "main": ".opencode/plugins/entire.js"
}
```

**.entire/settings.json**:
```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "telemetry": true
}
```

### 9. Directory Structure

```
/plugins/entire/
  ├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json
  ├── .codex-plugin/plugin.json
  └── /skills/
      ├── /explain/SKILL.md
      ├── /search/SKILL.md
      └── /session-handoff/SKILL.md

/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json
/.claude/
  ├── settings.json (hooks configuration)
  └── /agents/entire-search.md
/.codex/hooks.json
/.cursor-plugin/plugin.json
/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json
/.opencode/
  ├── INSTALL.md
  └── /plugins/entire.js
/gemini-extension.json
/GEMINI.md
```

### 10. Key Patterns Observed

1. **Skills are simple, single-purpose**: Each SKILL.md is self-contained with clear frontmatter and procedural instructions.

2. **No agents or references subdirectories under skills**: Skills contain only SKILL.md files. Agents/subagents are defined in `.claude/agents/` at the repo root level.

3. **Plugin configuration varies by agent type**: Each agent (Claude, Codex, Cursor) has a separate plugin.json with format-specific fields. Codex includes `interface` metadata; Cursor includes `displayName`.

4. **Hook configuration is agent-specific**: Claude Code uses detailed hooks (6 types: Pre/Post/Session/Stop/Submit). Codex uses 3 hooks with timeouts. Hooks call `entire` CLI commands.

5. **Marketplace discovery pattern**: Multiple marketplaces (.agents, .claude-plugin) point to the same local ./plugins/entire path with consistent naming.

6. **OpenCode uses ES modules**: Plugin hooks are JavaScript files with async config functions that manipulate the config object.

7. **Gemini uses file references**: GEMINI.md uses `@` syntax to include SKILL.md files directly.

This structure enables a single set of skills to be installed across 5+ different agent types while maintaining clean separation of agent-specific configuration.

Reference\n\nDetailed protocol for turn execution with fencing, snapshots, and diff computation.\n\n## Fencing Protocol\n\nThe `turn.version` field is a fencing token. It is incremented on every CLAIM and HANDOFF. The check is best-effort (read-then-write on a plain file, not truly atomic), but the race window is milliseconds against a ~60s poll interval — practically safe.\n\n### CLAIM Procedure\n\n```\n1. READ state.json → record turn.version as V\n2. VERIFY: turn.agent == my_type OR lease expired\n   - Lease expired = (now - turn.started_at) > turn.lease_seconds\n3. If neither condition met → not my turn, stop\n4. RE-READ state.json → check turn.version still equals V\n5. If version changed → another agent claimed first, back off\n6. WRITE state.json:\n   - turn.agent = my_type\n   - turn.started_at = <now ISO 8601>\n   - turn.version = V + 1\n7. Record V + 1 as my_version (needed for HANDOFF check)\n```\n\nIf reclaiming an expired turn, first append an expired entry to history:\n```json\n{\"turn\": <N>, \"agent\": \"<original_agent>\", \"expired\": true, \"timestamp\": \"<now>\"}\n```\n\n### HANDOFF Procedure\n\n```\n1. RE-READ state.json → check turn.version == my_version\n2. If version changed → ABORT\n   - Edits remain in the document file (not lost)\n   - Do NOT update state.json\n   - Report: \"Turn was reclaimed while editing. Edits are in the file but not in collab state.\"\n3. COPY document to snapshots/turn-<N>.md\n   *** SNAPSHOT MUST BE WRITTEN BEFORE STATE UPDATE ***\n4. WRITE state.json:\n   - Append to history[]: {turn, agent, snapshot path, summary, timestamp}\n   - turn.agent = next in turn_order (round-robin wrap)\n   - turn.number += 1\n   - turn.version += 1\n   - Increment my agents[].turns_completed\n5. CHECK termination:\n   - If config.max_turns != null AND turn.number > config.max_turns:\n     - Set status = \"completed\"\n     - Delete snapshots directory\n```\n\n### Write Ordering Rationale\n\nSnapshot is ALWAYS written before state.json. Partial failure scenarios:\n\n| Crash point | Snapshot | State | Recovery |\n|-------------|----------|-------|----------|\n| After snapshot, before state | Exists (orphaned) | Points to previous turn | Harmless — orphaned file cleaned up on /collab stop |\n| After state, before snapshot | Impossible | — | Snapshot is written first |\n| Both succeed | Exists | Updated | Normal operation |\n\n## Diff Computation\n\nTo show the next agent what changed:\n\n```bash\n# If previous snapshot exists:\ndiff .entire/collab/<id>/snapshots/turn-<N-1>.md <document_path> || true\n\n# If snapshot is missing (first turn or partial crash):\n# Skip diff — present full document content instead\n```\n\nThe `|| true` prevents diff from failing with exit code 1 when files differ (which is expected).\n\n## History Validation\n\nOn READ, before proceeding with a turn, validate:\n\n- `history` array length should equal `turn.number - 1`\n- Each `history[i].turn` should equal `i + 1` (monotonically increasing)\n\nIf validation fails: alert the user with the specific mismatch. Ask whether to continue or abort. Do NOT silently proceed with inconsistent state.\n\n## Lease Expiry\n\nA turn is expired when: `current_time - turn.started_at > turn.lease_seconds`\n\nThe lease protects against: agent crashes, closed terminals, network issues, agents taking too long.\n\nWhen an expired turn is reclaimed:\n1. The reclaiming agent follows normal CLAIM (with fencing check)\n2. An `\"expired\": true` entry is added to history for the original turn\n3. The document may contain partial edits from the expired agent — the reclaiming agent works from whatever state the file is in\n4. If the original agent later tries to HANDOFF, its version check fails and it aborts gracefully\n````\n\n- [ ] **Step 2: Verify**\n\n```bash\nhead -3 plugins/entire/skills/collab/references/turn-protocol.md\n```\n\nExpected: `# Turn Protocol Reference`\n\n- [ ] **Step 3: Commit**\n\n```bash\ngit add plugins/entire/skills/collab/references/turn-protocol.md\ngit commit -m \"feat: add turn-protocol.md reference for collab skill\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### Task 4: Create agents/collab-worker.md\n\n**Files:**\n- Create: `plugins/entire/skills/collab/agents/collab-worker.md`\n\nSubagent dispatched in orchestrator mode for non-Codex agents. Receives turn context, edits the document, writes snapshot, updates state.\n\n- [ ] **Step 1: Create the agents directory**\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p plugins/entire/skills/collab/agents\n```\n\n- [ ] **Step 2: Write collab-worker.md**\n\nCreate `plugins/entire/skills/collab/agents/collab-worker.md` with the following content:\n\n````markdown\n---\nname: collab-worker\ndescription: Execute a single collaboration turn on a shared document. Used by the collab skill in orchestrator mode to dispatch turns to agents via the Agent tool.\ntools: Read, Edit, Write, Bash\n---\n\n# Collaboration Turn Worker\n\nYou are executing a single turn in a multi-agent document collaboration. Follow these steps exactly.\n\n## Input\n\nYou will receive these values in your prompt:\n- `document_path` — the file to edit\n- `collab_dir` — the `.entire/collab/<id>` directory\n- `turn_number` — your turn number\n- `my_version` — the turn.version value set during CLAIM (verify this before updating state)\n- `role` — your editing directive (or \"Improve the document\")\n- `diff` — what changed in the previous turn (may be empty for first turn)\n- `history_summaries` — summaries of all previous turns\n- `next_agent` — the agent type to hand off to after your turn\n- `agent_type` — your agent type identifier\n\n## Procedure\n\n### 1. Read the document\nRead the full file at `document_path`.\n\n### 2. Review context\nConsider:\n- The diff showing what the previous agent changed\n- The history summaries for overall progression\n- Your role directive\n\n### 3. Edit the document\nMake substantive improvements guided by your role. Use the Edit tool to modify `document_path`.\n\n### 4. Write a summary\nCompose a one-line summary of what you changed. Be specific: \"Added error handling section with retry backoff semantics\" not \"Made improvements\".\n\n### 5. Write the snapshot\n```bash\ncp <document_path> <collab_dir>/snapshots/turn-<turn_number>.md\n```\n\n### 6. Verify fencing\nRead `<collab_dir>/state.json`. Check that `turn.version` equals `my_version`.\n\nIf version does NOT match:\n- Report: \"Turn was reclaimed. My edits are in the file but I cannot update state.\"\n- STOP here. Do not update state.json.\n\n### 7. Update state.json\nRead the current state.json, then write the updated version:\n- Append to `history[]`: `{\"turn\": <turn_number>, \"agent\": \"<agent_type>\", \"snapshot\": \"snapshots/turn-<turn_number>.md\", \"summary\": \"<your summary>\", \"timestamp\": \"<now ISO 8601>\"}`\n- Set `turn.agent` to `<next_agent>`\n- Increment `turn.number` by 1\n- Increment `turn.version` by 1\n- Find your entry in `agents[]` and increment `turns_completed` by 1\n\n### 8. Check termination\nIf `config.max_turns` is not null and the new `turn.number` exceeds it:\n- Set `status` to `\"completed\"`\n- Run: `rm -rf <collab_dir>/snapshots/`\n\n### 9. Report back\nReturn your one-line summary. The orchestrator will pick it up.\n\n## Rules\n\n- Do NOT commit any changes to git\n- Do NOT modify files other than `document_path` and `state.json`\n- Do NOT proceed past step 6 if the fencing check fails\n- Keep edits focused on your role — do not go on tangents\n- Write a specific, descriptive summary\n````\n\n- [ ] **Step 3: Verify**\n\n```bash\nhead -5 plugins/entire/skills/collab/agents/collab-worker.md\n```\n\nExpected: YAML frontmatter with `name: collab-worker`.\n\n- [ ] **Step 4: Commit**\n\n```bash\ngit add 0	# Collab Skill — Multi-Agent Document Collaboration
1	
2	**Date:** 2026-04-14
3	**Status:** Draft
4	**Author:** Alisha Kawaguchi + Claude
5	
6	## Overview
7	
8	A skill that enables multiple AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, etc.) to collaboratively author and refine a shared document through turn-based editing. Agents take short turns — one writes while the other reads/thinks — creating a sense of concurrency. The user can steer, pause, redirect, and stop the collaboration at any time, and other skills remain fully usable throughout.
9	
10	## Requirements
11	
12	- **Concurrent collaboration** with turn-based short leases — one agent writes while the other reads/thinks
13	- **Two modes**: single orchestrator (one terminal) or dual session (two terminals, shared protocol)
14	- **Single markdown file** as the shared document
15	- **General-purpose** — any document type, not just specs
16	- **Optional role assignment** at kickoff, with ability to interject/redirect mid-session
17	- **Agent-agnostic** — works with any agent that has file read/write and shell access
18	- **Termination**: fixed turn count or user-controlled stop
19	- **Non-blocking** — must coexist with other skills (brainstorming, etc.) within the same session
20	- **Uses existing Entire CLI infrastructure** — temporary checkpoints, session state, hooks
21	- **No commits required during collaboration** — user commits when satisfied
22	
23	## Architecture: Hybrid State File + Checkpoints
24

95	    - Did I follow TDD if required?
96	    - Are tests comprehensive?
97	
98	    If you find issues during self-review, fix them now before reporting.
99	
100	    ## Report Format
101	
102	    When done, report:
103	    - **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT

105	    - What you tested and test results
106	    - Files changed

110	    Use DONE_WITH_CONCERNS if you completed the work but have doubts about correctness.
111	    Use BLOCKED if you cannot complete the task. Use NEEDS_CONTEXT if you need

**Minor issue — CLAIM step ordering in Turn Execution Flow:** Step 3 says to append the expired entry to `history[]` during CLAIM _before_ the fencing re-read (step 4). This means the expired history write happens before the version check. However, turn-protocol.md correctly places the expired history write _after_ the re-read + version verification in the CLAIM procedure. The SKILL.md CLAIM steps are: (1) read V, (2) verify it's my turn or lease expired, (3) if expired append history entry, (4) re-read and verify V, (5) if changed back off. This means the expired history entry could be written _before_ confirming no race occurred — a minor ordering inconsistency vs. the reference protocol, which places the expired entry append after the version check passes.

**Non-blocking / ScheduleWakeup:** Present and correct (Check Flow step 4).

**Directory path `.entire/collab/<id>/`:** Correct throughout — not `.collab/`.

**Notes section:** Correctly describes gitignore behavior, fencing token, append-only history, and plain-file snapshots.

**No frontmatter:** Matches the plan — reference files don't need frontmatter.

---

## turn-protocol.md

**Fencing protocol language:** Correctly uses "best-effort (read-then-write on a plain file, not truly atomic)" — matches the spec's requirement for honest language.

**CLAIM procedure:** All 7 steps present and correct. Expired turn history entry correctly appended _after_ the version check (step 4 verify, then expired entry). This is consistent with the spec.

**HANDOFF procedure:** All 5 steps present. Snapshot written before state update — explicit `*** SNAPSHOT MUST BE WRITTEN BEFORE STATE UPDATE ***` note present. Matches spec.

**Write ordering rationale table:** Present and accurate — covers all three crash scenarios.

**Diff computation:** Uses `diff ... || true` on snapshot files (not git hash-object). Graceful fallback for missing snapshot (present full document). Matches spec.

**History validation:** Both checks present — length equals `turn.number - 1`, and each `history[i].turn` equals `i + 1` (monotonically increasing). Matches spec requirement exactly.

**Lease expiry:** All 4 points present — fencing check, expired history entry, partial edits handled gracefully, late HANDOFF fails version check. Matches spec.

---

## collab-worker.md

**Frontmatter:** `name: collab-worker`, `description`, `tools: Read, Edit, Write, Bash` — all present.

**9-step procedure:** All steps present — (1) read document, (2) review context, (3) edit document, (4) write summary, (5) write snapshot, (6) verify fencing, (7) update state.json, (8) check termination, (9) report back.

**Critical ordering issue:** Steps 5 (write snapshot) and 6 (verify fencing) are in the wrong order relative to the spec. The collab-worker writes the snapshot BEFORE verifying the fencing token. The spec (design spec, HANDOFF procedure, turn-protocol.md) requires: (1) verify fencing first, THEN (2) write snapshot, THEN (3) update state. The collab-worker does: (5) write snapshot, then (6) verify fencing, then (7) update state. This means if the fencing check fails, the snapshot has already been written as an orphan — which is harmless per the spec's crash analysis, but it's inconsistent with the SKILL.md HANDOFF which checks fencing before copying. More importantly, in the design spec's HANDOFF description: "Before writing the handoff, agent re-reads state.json and verifies it still owns the turn... If the version matches, the agent: first copies the document..." — the fencing check must come before the snapshot.

**Rules section:** All 5 rules present and correct.

The collab-worker is inverted. While orphaned snapshots are harmless, this contradicts the stated protocol ordering in both the design spec and turn-protocol.md.

2. **`SKILL.md` CLAIM step 3 vs turn-protocol.md (SKILL.md:203–204):** In the Turn Execution Flow CLAIM section, step 3 appends the expired history entry before the re-read/version check (step 4). The reference protocol in turn-protocol.md correctly places the expired entry append after the version is confirmed unchanged. This means SKILL.md could write an expired history entry even if the version check then fails and backs off — leaving a spurious expired entry. The fix: move the expired entry append to after step 4's version confirmation (between steps 5 and 6, i.e., only append after confirming you can claim).

I now have a thorough understanding of all four files, the commit history, and the existing skill conventions. Here is my review.

---

## Collab Skill Review

### Strengths

**Well-designed protocol architecture.** The fencing token scheme using `turn.version` with read-verify-write is a pragmatic concurrency control for a file-based coordination system. The write-ordering rationale in `turn-protocol.md` (lines 52-60) is particularly strong -- the crash-safety analysis table clearly explains why snapshots must precede state updates, and every partial-failure scenario is accounted for.

**Excellent cross-document consistency.** The CLAIM and HANDOFF procedures in SKILL.md (lines 200-268), turn-protocol.md (lines 9-50), and collab-worker.md (steps 5-7) all describe the same protocol with matching field names, step ordering, and semantics. The fix in commit `f08e7dd` correctly addressed the two ordering bugs (expired history append placement and fencing-before-snapshot in the worker), and the current state is consistent across all three documents.

**Strong error handling throughout.** Every flow accounts for failure cases: version conflicts during CLAIM, lease expiry recovery, missing snapshots on READ, history length mismatches, collab-not-found on JOIN, and graceful abort on HANDOFF version mismatch. The agent is never left in a state where it would not know what to do.

**Good use of the STOP block convention.** The "STOP -- Critical Protocol Rules" section at the top of SKILL.md matches the established pattern in session-handoff's "STOP -- Read these rules before doing ANYTHING" block. This is the right way to front-load invariants that an LLM must not violate.

**Non-blocking design is clearly communicated.** The explicit statement on SKILL.md line 10 and the `/loop /collab check` integration with ScheduleWakeup (lines 185-188) make it clear this is a polling-based system that does not hold the session hostage.

---

### Issues

#### Critical

None found. The protocol is internally consistent, the fencing logic is correct, and there are no flows where the agent would deadlock or silently corrupt state.

#### Important

**1. History validation breaks on expired turns (SKILL.md line 221, turn-protocol.md line 80).**

The READ phase validates that `history.length == turn.number - 1`. However, when a turn expires (CLAIM step 5, SKILL.md line 258), an `expired` entry is appended to history *without incrementing `turn.number`*. After one expired turn reclaim, history will have N entries but `turn.number` will still be N (because the expired turn did not complete and advance the counter). The very next READ will see `history.length == turn.number` and flag a mismatch, prompting the user with a warning every time someone reclaims an expired turn.

The fix is either: (a) document that expired entries are excluded from the length check (e.g., "history entries where `expired != true` should equal `turn.number - 1`"), or (b) change the validation to count only non-expired entries.

**2. Pause flow lacks fencing -- can pause mid-turn (SKILL.md lines 329-333).**

The Pause flow reads state.json, sets `status = "paused"`, and writes. There is no version check. If agent A is in the middle of an EDIT phase and the user runs `/collab pause` in another terminal, state.json is overwritten without incrementing `turn.version`. When agent A reaches HANDOFF and re-reads state.json, its version check *might* still pass (since pause did not touch `turn.version`), but now `status` is `"paused"` while a turn is being committed. The Resume and Stop flows have the same pattern.

Recommendation: either increment `turn.version` in Pause/Resume/Stop (so an in-flight HANDOFF detects the change and aborts cleanly), or document explicitly that these commands should only be run when no turn is actively executing. The latter is simpler and probably sufficient for v1.

**3. collab-worker.md does not instruct the subagent to handle `my_version` correctly for reclaim scenarios (collab-worker.md lines 17, 42-45).**

The worker receives `my_version` as an input parameter and checks it at step 5. But the orchestrator (SKILL.md Orchestrator Loop, lines 274-298) does the CLAIM itself and then dispatches the worker. The SKILL.md instructions for building the Codex prompt (line 287) say "Edit the file ... copy it to snapshot ... update state.json" but do not mention passing `my_version`. Only the collab-worker.md input spec mentions `my_version`. This creates an inconsistency: the Codex dispatch path in SKILL.md does not mention the fencing token, which means a Codex agent following those inline instructions would skip the HANDOFF version check entirely.

Recommendation: add `my_version` to the Codex dispatch prompt template in the Orchestrator Loop (SKILL.md line 287), and explicitly state: "Before writing snapshot or state, verify `turn.version == <my_version>`. If it changed, stop."

**4. Snapshot file extension is hardcoded to `.md` (SKILL.md line 256, collab-worker.md line 50).**

The snapshot copy is always `turn-<N>.md`, but the `document_path` could be any file type (`.txt`, `.rst`, `.adoc`, etc.). If the user starts a collab on `design.txt`, the snapshot will be saved as `turn-1.md`, which is misleading and could cause issues if any downstream logic infers format from the extension.

Recommendation: use the original file's extension in the snapshot name (e.g., `turn-<N>.<ext>`), or use no extension at all since these are just backup copies.

#### Minor

**5. Frontmatter style inconsistency with existing skills.**

The existing skills use different frontmatter keys:
- `session-handoff/SKILL.md`: `description` only
- `explain/SKILL.md`: `description`, `argument-hint`
- `search/SKILL.md`: `description` only

The collab skill uses `description` and `argument-hint`, which matches explain. This is fine. However, the collab `description` value (SKILL.md line 2) is significantly longer than any existing skill -- 336 characters spanning multiple trigger phrases. The other skills keep descriptions to 1-2 sentences. While this may help with triggering accuracy, it is worth noting for consistency.

**6. No guidance for what happens when `/collab start` is run while a collaboration on the same document is already active (SKILL.md Start Flow).**

The Start flow creates a new collab ID and initializes fresh state regardless of existing collabs. If a user accidentally runs `/collab start docs/design.md` twice, they get two independent collabs on the same document with no warning. The Join flow checks for existing collabs, but Start does not.

Recommendation: add a check at the beginning of Start flow: search for existing active collabs on the same `document_path`. If found, warn the user and ask if they want to join the existing one instead.

**7. The `entire sessions list` command fallback is underspecified (SKILL.md line 65-67).**

The instruction says "Parse the output to find your agent type" but does not describe the output format of `entire sessions list` or how to extract the agent type from it. The fallback "default to claude-code if running in Claude Code" is good, but an LLM encountering unfamiliar CLI output may misparse it. Consider adding an example of the expected output format, or at least specifying which field to look for.

**8. The `collab-worker.md` Rules section says "Do NOT proceed past step 6" (line 72) but should say "Do NOT proceed past step 5".**

Step 5 is "Verify fencing" and the instruction within step 5 already says "STOP here. Do not write the snapshot or update state.json." The rule at line 72 saying "Do NOT proceed past step 6 if the fencing check fails" is contradictory -- if the fencing check fails at step 5, you should stop at step 5, not proceed through step 6 (Write the snapshot) before stopping. The commit `f08e7dd` fixed the ordering of steps 5 and 6 but did not update this rule to match.

**9. Turn-protocol.md CLAIM expired entry placement is ambiguous (line 26-28).**

The turn-protocol says "If reclaiming an expired turn, first append an expired entry to history" with the word "first" suggesting it happens before the WRITE step. But the SKILL.md CLAIM (after the fix in `f08e7dd`) places it at step 5, which is *after* the re-read/version-check at steps 3-4 but *before* the write at step 6. The turn-protocol's "first" could be misread as "before everything else." Consider changing the wording to: "After verifying the version (step 5), and before writing state (step 6), append an expired entry..."

---

### Assessment

This is a well-structured, thorough skill implementation. The core protocol design is sound -- the fencing token, write ordering, lease expiry, and crash recovery are all thoughtfully engineered. The four-file decomposition (main skill, schema reference, protocol reference, subagent) is a good architectural choice that keeps the main file focused on flows while extracting reusable protocol details.

The most actionable item is **issue 1** (history validation vs. expired entries), which will cause false warnings in a common scenario. **Issue 3** (missing `my_version` in Codex dispatch) and **issue 8** (wrong step number in collab-worker rules) are straightforward fixes. The remaining items are hardening suggestions rather than blockers.

**Relevant files:**
- `/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/skills/experiment/plugins/entire/skills/collab/SKILL.md`
- `/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/skills/experiment/plugins/entire/skills/collab/references/state-schema.md`
- `/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/skills/experiment/plugins/entire/skills/collab/references/turn-protocol.md`
- `/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/skills/experiment/plugins/entire/skills/collab/agents/collab-worker.md`

> AGENT

**Dual-session mode: Yes, works fine.** Each agent runs independently in its own terminal. No cross-dependencies.

**Orchestrator mode: No, it has a gap.** The dispatch section hardcodes `codex:rescue` for Codex agents with no fallback. If the plugin isn't installed, the agent would try to invoke it and fail. There's no guard like "if codex:rescue is not available, fall back to collab-worker subagent or manual trigger."

The fix is straightforward — add a fallback chain to the dispatch section:

1. **Try `codex:rescue`** if available (uses GPT-5.4 via companion script)
2. **Fall back to `collab-worker` subagent** via Agent tool (uses Claude, not Codex — different model but still works)
3. **Fall back to manual trigger** (tell user to run `/collab check` in another terminal)

This also applies to any agent type that might have a specialized dispatch path in the future. Want me to fix this?

## Report: Codex Task Dispatch Mechanism

Based on my thorough exploration of the Codex plugin, here's the complete task dispatching architecture:

### 1. **Task Subcommand Signature**

**Invocation:**
```bash
node scripts/codex-companion.mjs task [--background] [--write] [--resume-last|--resume|--fresh] [--model <model|spark>] [--effort <none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh>] [prompt]
```

### 2. **Prompt/Task Input Acceptance**

The `task` subcommand accepts prompts in three ways:
- **Positional argument:** `task "Fix the login bug"`
- **Prompt file:** `task --prompt-file ./prompt.txt`
- **Piped stdin:** `echo "Fix the bug" | task`

The prompt parsing occurs in `readTaskPrompt()` (lines 585-592), which tries in order: prompt-file, positionals, then piped stdin.

### 3. **Flag Support**

**Boolean flags:**
- `--write`: Enables **write mode** (sandbox: "workspace-write"). Default is read-only.
- `--background`: Queues the task asynchronously instead of blocking
- `--resume-last` / `--resume`: Continues the previous task thread
- `--fresh`: Forces a new task (incompatible with `--resume-last`)
- `--json`: Returns JSON output instead of rendered text

**Value flags:**
- `--model <name>`: Specify model (e.g., `gpt-5-4-prompting`, or `spark` alias for `gpt-5.3-codex-spark`)
- `--effort <level>`: Reasoning effort: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`
- `--cwd <path>`: Working directory (alias: `-C`)

### 4. **Codex Session Launch**

**Foreground execution** (default, synchronous):
1. `handleTask()` parses flags and validates input (lines 704-765)
2. Calls `executeTaskRun()` which:
   - Resolves any resume thread ID if `--resume-last` is set
   - Calls `runAppServerTurn()` (codex.mjs, lines 829-894) which:
     - Connects to the Codex app-server via `CodexAppServerClient.connect()`
     - Starts or resumes a thread
     - Submits the prompt with sandbox mode (`read-only` or `workspace-write`)
     - Captures turn progress via `captureTurn()` notification handler
     - Returns when turn completes

**Background execution** (with `--background`):
1. `enqueueBackgroundTask()` spawns a detached worker process (lines 613-624):
   ```javascript
   spawn(process.execPath, [scriptPath, "task-worker", "--cwd", cwd, "--job-id", jobId], {
     detached: true,
     stdio: "ignore"
   })
   ```
2. Job record written to disk with status `"queued"` 
3. Returns immediately with `jobId` and log file path

The worker process runs the same `executeTaskRun()` logic independently.

### 5. **Result Return Mechanism**

**Result object structure** (lines 480-498):
```javascript
{
  exitStatus: 0 or 1,           // Codex turn status
  threadId: string,              // Thread ID (persisted for --resume-last)
  turnId: string,                // Turn ID (for interrupt/cancel)
  payload: {
    status: number,
    threadId: string,
    rawOutput: string,            // Final assistant message
    touchedFiles: string[],        // Files modified (only with --write)
    reasoningSummary: string[]     // Reasoning traces from model
  },
  rendered: string,              // Human-readable formatted output
  summary: string,               // First meaningful line
  jobTitle: string,              // "Codex Task", "Codex Resume", or "Codex Stop Gate Review"
  jobClass: "task",
  write: boolean
}
```

**Output formats:**
- **Foreground, rendered (default):** Human-readable text via `renderTaskResult()`
- **Foreground, JSON:** `--json` flag returns structured payload
- **Background:** Returns queued status with `jobId`, user polls with `status` subcommand

### 6. **Supporting Subcommands for Task Management**

- **`status [job-id]`**: Check job progress (queued/running/completed)
- **`result [job-id]`**: Retrieve completed task result
- **`cancel [job-id]`**: Cancel running task (attempts `turn/interrupt` via app-server)

### 7. **Gemini Equivalent: No Direct Task Dispatch**

**Critical finding:** Gemini CLI has **NO equivalent to Codex's task dispatch mechanism**.

From `/Users/alisha/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/5.0.7/skills/using-superpowers/references/gemini-tools.md`:

> | Skill references | Gemini CLI equivalent |
> |---|---|
> | `Task` tool (dispatch subagent) | **No equivalent — Gemini CLI does not support subagents** |

Gemini CLI limitations:
- No subagent/task dispatch at all
- No persistent thread management
- No background job queuing
- Skills that rely on subagent work fall back to single-session execution via `executing-plans`

### 8. **Key Implementation Details**

**Thread persistence** (line 462):
- `persistThread: true` causes the thread to be saved for later resume
- Thread names are auto-generated from first line of prompt: `buildPersistentTaskThreadName()`
- Only task threads (not ephemeral turns) are searchable for `--resume-last`

**Sandbox isolation** (line 460):
- `sandbox: request.write ? "workspace-write" : "read-only"`
- Write mode explicitly required; default is read-only

**Default continue prompt** (line 457):
- If resuming without explicit prompt: "Continue from the current thread state. Pick the next highest-value step and follow through until the task is resolved."

**Model aliasing** (lines 100-109):
- `spark` normalizes to `gpt-5.3-codex-spark`
- Other model names pass through unchanged

---

**Bottom line:** Codex provides a complete job dispatch system with foreground/background execution, persistent threads, and structured result return. Gemini CLI is single-session only—no equivalent mechanism exists.
```

## Analysis Report: Claude Code Permission Configuration for `.entire/collab/`

Based on my exploration of your configuration files, I can now provide you with the exact syntax and patterns for auto-approving file operations.

### Key Findings:

**1. Current Configuration in `/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/skills/experiment/.claude/settings.json`:**
- Has a deny rule that blocks reads to `./.entire/metadata/**`
- Does NOT have allow rules for Write or Bash operations

**2. Global User Settings (`/Users/alisha/.claude/settings.json`):**
- Uses two permission styles:
  - **Command-based Bash permissions:** `"Bash(command:*)"` - allows commands matching a pattern with wildcard
  - **Path-based Read permissions:** `"Read(/Users/alisha/Projects/**)"` - allows reading from path patterns with `**` glob support
  - **Skill and MCP permissions:** `"Skill(name:action)"` and `"mcp__*"` for tools

**3. Permission Pattern Syntax Found:**
- For Read with paths: `"Read(/path/to/dir/**)"` - recursive glob pattern
- For Bash with commands: `"Bash(command:*)"` - command prefix matching
- For denying: Same syntax used in `"deny"` array

**4. Examples from User Settings:**
- `"Read(/Users/alisha/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/**)"` - absolute paths
- `"Read(/Users/alisha/Projects/**)"` - directory patterns with glob
- `"Bash(git add:*)"`, `"Bash(npm run:*)"`, `"Bash(cargo:*)"` - command patterns

### JSON Configuration for Auto-Approving `.entire/collab/`

Here is the exact JSON to add to `/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/skills/experiment/.claude/settings.json` to auto-approve Write and Bash operations on `.entire/collab/` paths:

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Write(./.entire/collab/**)",
      "Bash(* ./.entire/collab/*)",
      "Read(./.entire/collab/**)"
    ],
    "deny": [
      "Read(./.entire/metadata/**)"
    ]
  }
}
```

**Or, if using absolute paths:**

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Write(/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/skills/experiment/.entire/collab/**)",
      "Bash(* /Users/alisha/Projects/wt/skills/experiment/.entire/collab/*)",
      "Read(/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/skills/experiment/.entire/collab/**)"
    ],
    "deny": [
      "Read(./.entire/metadata/**)"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Important Notes:

1. **Permission Styles:**
   - Path-based permissions use glob patterns with `**` for recursive matching
   - Relative paths (`./.entire/`) work in project-level settings
   - Absolute paths work in both global and project settings

2. **No PermissionRequest Hook for Auto-Approval:**
   - The global settings have a `PermissionRequest` hook, but it only calls an external notify script
   - There is NO built-in hook mechanism to auto-approve permissions based on patterns
   - The `allow` array in permissions is the ONLY way to auto-approve operations

3. **Bash Permission Pattern:**
   - For Bash with path arguments, use wildcard pattern like `"Bash(* /path/**)"` to allow any command with paths in that directory
   - The default patterns like `"Bash(git add:*)"` match the command name and allow any arguments

4. **Deny Takes Precedence:**
   - If a path matches both `allow` and `deny`, the `deny` rule wins
   - Your current deny of `./.entire/metadata/**` won't conflict with `./.entire/collab/**`

### File Location to Edit:
`/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/skills/experiment/.claude/settings.json`

This is where the project-specific permission overrides are configured. Adding the `allow` array will auto-approve those operations without prompting.

# Collab Skill: Dispatch Script + Auto-Approve Permissions

## Context

Two issues with the collab skill in orchestrator mode:

1. **Codex dispatch depends on `codex:rescue` skill** — if the user doesn't have the codex plugin installed, orchestrator mode can't dispatch to Codex. We need the collab skill to handle dispatch itself, with fallbacks.

2. **Every `.entire/collab/` file operation prompts for approval** — writing state.json, copying snapshots, creating directories all trigger permission prompts. These should be auto-approved since `.entire/` is the skill's own coordination directory.

Additionally: Gemini CLI has NO task dispatch mechanism (confirmed from exploration), so Gemini always falls back to manual trigger in dual-session mode.

## Changes

### 1. Add `scripts/dispatch.sh` — agent dispatch wrapper

**File:** `plugins/entire/skills/collab/scripts/dispatch.sh`

A bash script that dispatches a collaboration turn to an external agent:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Usage: dispatch.sh <agent-type> <prompt-file> [--cwd <dir>]
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 = success
#   1 = agent not found or dispatch failed
#   2 = unsupported agent type

AGENT_TYPE="$1"
PROMPT_FILE="$2"
CWD="."
if [ "$3" = "--cwd" ] && [ -n "$4" ]; then CWD="$4"; fi

case "$AGENT_TYPE" in
  codex)
    # Try codex companion script (from installed plugin)
    COMPANION=$(find ~/.claude/plugins -path "*/codex/*/scripts/codex-companion.mjs" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
    if [ -n "$COMPANION" ]; then
      node "$COMPANION" task --write --cwd "$CWD" "$(cat "$PROMPT_FILE")"
      exit $?
    fi
    # Try codex CLI directly
    if command -v codex &>/dev/null; then
      codex --approval-mode full-auto --quiet "$(cat "$PROMPT_FILE")"
      exit $?
    fi
    echo "codex-not-found"
    exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "unsupported-agent"
    exit 2
    ;;
esac
```

- Only handles Codex for now (Gemini has no task dispatch API)
- Tries companion script first (richer integration), falls back to raw CLI
- Returns structured exit codes so SKILL.md can decide fallback

### 2. Update SKILL.md — Orchestrator dispatch with fallback chain

**File:** `plugins/entire/skills/collab/SKILL.md` (lines ~288-299)

Replace the hardcoded `codex:rescue` dispatch with a fallback chain:

```markdown
**4. Dispatch:**

Write the turn prompt to a temp file:
\`\`\`bash
cat > /tmp/collab-turn-prompt.txt << 'PROMPT'
<full turn prompt here, including my_version and all instructions>
PROMPT
\`\`\`

- **Codex:** Try the dispatch script first:
  \`\`\`bash
  bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/dispatch.sh codex /tmp/collab-turn-prompt.txt --cwd $(pwd)
  \`\`\`
  If the script returns exit code 1 (codex not found), fall back to the `collab-worker` subagent via the Agent tool.
  If it returns exit code 0, read state.json to verify the turn was recorded.

- **Any other agent (Gemini, Cursor, etc.):** These agents don't support programmatic dispatch. Tell the user:
  > "Next turn is `<agent_type>`. Please trigger it in their terminal with `/collab check`."
  Then poll state.json until the turn is recorded, or wait for user confirmation.

- **Claude Code (self-dispatch):** Use the Agent tool with the `collab-worker` subagent.
```

### 3. Update SKILL.md — Use Write tool instead of Bash cp for snapshots

Replace `cp` commands with Write tool usage so path-based permissions work:

- **HANDOFF step 3**: Instead of `cp <doc> .entire/collab/<id>/snapshots/turn-<N>.<ext>`, instruct: "Read the document content, then use the Write tool to write it to the snapshot path"
- **Stop flow cleanup**: Keep `rm -rf` via Bash (needs Bash permission)
- **Diff computation**: Standardize as `diff .entire/collab/<id>/snapshots/turn-<N-1>.<ext> <document_path>` (snapshot path first, so Bash permission prefix matches)

### 4. Add auto-approve permissions to `.claude/settings.json`

**File:** `plugins/entire/skills/collab/.claude/settings.json` (new file — skill-level settings)

Wait — skills can't have their own settings.json. The permissions need to go in the project's `.claude/settings.json`.

**File:** `.claude/settings.json` — add to existing `permissions.allow` array:

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Write(.entire/collab/**)",
      "Read(.entire/collab/**)",
      "Bash(mkdir -p .entire:*)",
      "Bash(rm -rf .entire/collab:*)",
      "Bash(find .entire:*)",
      "Bash(diff .entire:*)",
      "Bash(head -c 4 /dev/urandom:*)",
      "Bash(grep -q .entire:*)"
    ],
    "deny": [
      "Read(./.entire/metadata/**)"
    ]
  }
}
```

### 5. Update collab-worker.md — Use Write tool for snapshots

Same change as SKILL.md: replace `cp` with Write tool instruction so it works with path permissions.

> AGENT

Done. Here's what changed:

**Dispatch script** (`scripts/dispatch.sh`):
- Tries Codex companion script first (from installed plugin at `~/.claude/plugins`)
- Falls back to `codex` CLI directly
- Returns structured exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = not found, 2 = unsupported agent
- Gemini/Cursor have no dispatch API — they always need manual trigger via `/collab check` in their own terminal

**SKILL.md orchestrator dispatch** — fallback chain:
1. Codex: dispatch script → collab-worker subagent → manual trigger
2. Claude Code: collab-worker subagent directly
3. Everything else: manual trigger (user runs `/collab check` in the agent's terminal)

**Snapshots** — now use Write tool instead of `cp`, so path-based auto-approve works

**Auto-approve permissions** in `.claude/settings.json`:
- `Write(.entire/collab/**)`, `Read(.entire/collab/**)` — state and snapshots
- `Bash(mkdir/rm/find/diff/head/grep)` for the shell commands the skill uses

> DEVELOPER

so if I have claude start designing something and it does a bunch of research it doesn't share that research with the other agents. is there a way to compact what it learned so that the other agents have some context when starting?

> AGENT

Great observation. Right now the turn prompt gives the next agent the document, a diff, and one-line summaries — that's not enough context for meaningful collaboration. Codex gets the *what* but not the *why*.

The simplest fix: add a **context file** alongside the document.

**How it would work:**

1. During `/collab start`, after the initiating agent's research/exploration but before turn 1, the skill prompts: *"Summarize what you've learned so far — codebase findings, design decisions, constraints — so other agents have context."*

2. This gets saved to `.entire/collab/<id>/context.md`

3. Every turn prompt includes this context file alongside the document and diff

4. Any agent can append to it during their turn if they discover something new

It's essentially a briefing document that travels with the collaboration — similar to how the session-handoff skill creates a compaction summary (task overview, discoveries, constraints, next steps).

The context file would look something like:

```markdown
## Codebase
- Auth middleware at src/middleware/auth.ts, uses JWT
- Database models use Prisma, migrations in prisma/migrations/

## Design Decisions
- Chose event sourcing over CRUD because of audit requirements
- API must stay backward-compatible with v1

## Constraints
- Deploy deadline is Friday
- Cannot modify the shared auth service
```

Small, focused, high-signal. Want me to add this to the skill?

Done. Here's how it works:

**On `/collab start`** — before turn 1, the skill prompts the initiating agent to write a context briefing to `.entire/collab/<id>/context.md`. This captures codebase findings, design decisions, constraints, and open questions from whatever research the agent did before starting the collab.

**On every turn** — the context.md contents are included in the turn prompt under "## Research Context", right after the role assignment and before the diff. So Codex (or any agent) starts its turn already knowing what Claude discovered.

**During any turn** — agents can append to context.md if they discover something new. The instruction is explicit: "If you discover something important, append it to the context file."

The context file is lightweight (bullets, not essays) and lives alongside state.json — ephemeral, gitignored, cleaned up when the collab ends.

would it be easier to use entire explain or summary or some new entire command or use agent handoff to do this instead of writing to context.md

Good instinct. The session-handoff skill already solves this problem — it reads the current session's full transcript and compacts it into a structured summary (task overview, discoveries, constraints, next steps). That's richer and more automatic than asking the agent to manually write context.md.

Here's the comparison:

| Approach | Pros | Cons |
|----------|------|------|
| **Manual context.md** (current) | Simple, agent controls what's shared | Agent forgets things, extra work, inconsistent |
| **Session handoff compaction** | Auto-generated from full transcript, captures everything the agent explored/reasoned about, already built | Designed for between-session handoff, not mid-session |
| **`entire explain`** | Works with checkpoints | Needs a commit, explains code not reasoning |
| **New `entire compact` command** | Purpose-built, cleanest API | Requires CLI changes, new feature to build |

**My recommendation:** Use session-handoff's compaction approach during `/collab start`. Instead of asking the agent to manually write context.md, the skill:

1. Reads the current session transcript (via `entire sessions info` → transcript path)
2. Compacts it into the 5-section format (task overview, current state, discoveries, next steps, context to preserve)
3. Saves the result as the context briefing

The agent didn't have to think about what to include — it's extracted from everything they actually did. And agents can still append during their turns.

The context.md file is still useful as the *storage format* — it's what other agents read. The change is in how it gets *populated*: auto-compaction from transcript instead of manual writing.
